newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower, tracking Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower, tracking Wall St.

text.p: Chilean shares closed a shade lower with the market dragged down by Wall Street's slide, said dealers.
The bolsa is seen opening weaker Thursday with investors keeping a close eye on the Dow's direction, they said.
"The bourse will probably react negatively tomorrow as a result of the Wall Street's retreat, although in the long-term Santiago has not tended to follow New York's tendency," said one broker.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.05 per cent at 111.7 points.
The general IGPA index shed 0.11 percent to 5,223.8 points amid volume of 9.3 billion pesos.
Leading decliners included steel-maker Cap which slumped five percent to 1,140 pesos on news the company's 1996 earnings fell nearly 20 percent last year, said dealers.
Rising issues included financial group Security Holdings which announced a 20 percent increase in earnings last year to 6.6 billion pesos.
Security ended up 2.56 percent at 400 pesos.
Declining issues included publishing firm Cochrane, down 5.74 percent at 115 pesos and forestry company Terranova which shed 4.76 percent to 400 pesos.
